title: Inoculating a Liquid Bacterial Culture
author: Saul Moore
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8rxhv7n

steps.title: Obtain LB broth
steps.instruction: Retrieve LB broth from the media kitchen; the broth contains 4 g NaCl, 4 g tryptone, 2 g yeast extract, and deionized water brought to a final volume of 400 mL.

steps.title: Transfer LB and add antibiotic
steps.instruction: Aliquot the liquid LB into the desired container (e.g., 2 mL into a 1.5 mL Falcon tube for a mini‑prep or up to 1 L into a 2 L Erlenmeyer flask for larger preparations) and add the required antibiotic at the concentration specified in the accompanying table.

substeps.instruction: Choose container size based on preparation scale (2 mL for mini‑prep, up to 1 L for larger prep).
Add antibiotic to the LB to achieve the correct final concentration.

steps.title: Inoculate culture with single colony
steps.instruction: Using a sterile inoculation loop, pick a single colony from a LB agar plate, dip the loop into the liquid LB, swirl to disperse cells, then discard the loop.

substeps.instruction: Select a single colony from the streaked LB agar plate with a sterile loop.
Dip the loop into the liquid LB and swirl gently.
Discard the inoculation loop in an appropriate biohazard container.

steps.title: Cover culture loosely
steps.instruction: Loosely cover the culture vessel with sterile aluminium foil or a cap that is not airtight to allow gas exchange.

steps.title: Incubate culture overnight
steps.instruction: Place the culture in a shaking incubator set to the required growth temperature and incubate for 12–18 hours (overnight).

substeps.instruction: Set shaking incubator to the appropriate temperature for the bacterial strain.

steps.title: Assess growth and measure OD600
steps.instruction: After incubation, verify growth by the appearance of a cloudy haze, then measure the optical density at 600 nm three times using a spectrophotometer with LB broth as the blank; calculate and record the average OD600.

substeps.instruction: Observe the culture for a cloudy haze indicating growth.
Measure OD600 three separate times, using LB broth as the blank.
Calculate the average of the three readings and record the value.
